questions.description: The only party where getting your clothes dirty isn't just allowed, it's the whole point.

I went to university to learn how to design buildings.

questions.fun_fact: Sanqingshan (三清山), a mountain in Jiangxi, is named after these gods because its three highest peaks are said to look like them sitting together.

questions.description: Some emperors build new capitals; this one just packed up and moved east.
questions.question: Emperor Guangwu of Han (汉光武帝) set up the Eastern Han capital in the province shown on this map. Which province is it?
hints: The Western Han capital Chang'an was further west, so it's not the same province.
This province sits in the middle of the Yellow River plain and is often called the cradle of Chinese civilization.
The Eastern Han capital was Luoyang, home of the Longmen Grottoes.
questions.fun_fact: Liu Xiu, later Emperor Guangwu, brought back the Han dynasty in 25 AD, after Wang Mang's short Xin dynasty.

media.author: Quintucket

questions.description: Bronze vessels, ritual music and very good manners: welcome to a dynasty that took ceremonies seriously.
questions.question: Around when did the Western Zhou (西周) dynasty begin?
hints: It came right after the Shang dynasty.
King Wu of Zhou founded it after his victory at Muye.
It's in the 11th century BC.
questions.fun_fact: Western Zhou ended in 771 BC, and the next year the capital moved east to Luoyang, which started the Eastern Zhou.

media.author: Gary Todd

questions.description: Two former allies, one empire up for grabs, and a chessboard that still remembers their fight.
questions.question: Xiang Yu and Liu Bang rebelled together and brought a dynasty down, then fought each other in the Chu–Han Contention (楚汉之争). Which dynasty did they bring down?
hints: This dynasty lasted only about 15 years.
It was the first dynasty to unify all of China.
Its founder built the Terracotta Army.
questions.fun_fact: The river across the middle of a Chinese chess board is called 楚河汉界 (Chǔ hé Hàn jiè, “Chu River, Han border”), after this war.

media.credit: Internet Archive Book Images · No restrictions · Wikimedia Commons
media.author: Internet Archive Book Images

questions.description: The most expensive smile in history: it cost a king his whole capital.
questions.question: King You lit the beacon fires just to make Bao Si laugh. Which era began soon after his fall?
hints: This era is known for great thinkers such as Confucius and Laozi.
It is often split into the Spring and Autumn and the Warring States periods.
After King You's fall, the court moved its capital east to Luoyi (洛邑).
questions.fun_fact: The story gave Chinese the idiom 烽火戏诸侯 (fēng huǒ xì zhū hóu, “playing tricks on the lords with beacon fires”), and the capital moved east in 770 BCE.

questions.description: Hunan's favourite home dish: so hot that the rice bowl calls for help.
questions.question: In the Hunan dish 辣椒炒肉 (làjiāo chǎo ròu, "stir-fried meat with chilli"), the name just says 肉. Which meat is it?
hints: In most Chinese dish names, 肉 on its own means the same everyday meat.
It's the meat in 红烧肉 (hóngshāo ròu) and in 回锅肉 (huíguō ròu) too.
This meat comes from the animal of the last year in the Chinese zodiac.
questions.fun_fact: Chillies only reached China from the Americas about 400 years ago, yet today Hunan is one of the spiciest places to eat in the world.

questions.question: Look at the photo: rice cooked in a clay pot, topped with sausage, with a crispy crust at the bottom. Which of the eight great cuisines is it from?
hints: It's a classic winter dish in the south of China and in Hong Kong.
The same cuisine is famous for dim sum and morning tea (早茶).
Its home province's capital is Guangzhou.
questions.fun_fact: The crispy rice crust at the bottom of the pot is called 饭焦 (fàn jiāo) in Cantonese, and many people scrape the pot to get every bit of it.

questions.description: Some say too much of a good thing is still a good thing. These farmers disagree.
questions.question: Long ago, ten of me rose in the sky together and the earth grew too hot. The archer Hou Yi shot down nine of us. What am I?
hints: Today there is only one of me left.
I give light and heat every day.
I rise in the east each morning.
questions.fun_fact: Hou Yi's wife is Chang'e (嫦娥), who in a famous legend flew to the moon, and China named its moon probes after her.

questions.description: Nature's crunchiest snack, with a panda on the other end.
questions.question: Pandas crunch bamboo stems all day long. Which of these is NOT true about bamboo stems?
hints: Think about where a bamboo stem comes from.
Three of these you could check by cutting or watching a bamboo stem.
Bamboo is actually a giant kind of grass.
questions.fun_fact: Bamboo is a giant grass, and some kinds can grow almost 1 m in a single day.

questions.description: Long before telescopes, a small child had a very creative guess about what was hanging in the night sky.
questions.question: Which Tang dynasty poet wrote 古朗月行 (gǔ lǎng yuè xíng), which starts “小时不识月，呼作白玉盘”?
hints: He loved wine and travelled all over China.
People call him the “Immortal of Poetry” (诗仙).
He also wrote 静夜思, the poem that starts “床前明月光”.
questions.fun_fact: In the poem, the child calls the moon a “white jade plate” (白玉盘) and wonders if it is a mirror flying above the clouds.

questions.description: Cash is feeling very lonely in its wallet these days.
questions.question: I was born in Japan in 1994 to keep track of car parts. Now I sit on almost every shop counter in China, and you scan me with your phone to pay. What am I?
hints: You need a phone camera to read me.
I'm a little square full of black and white dots.
Alipay and WeChat Pay show me on the screen too.
questions.fun_fact: The QR code was made by the Japanese company Denso Wave, and “QR” stands for “Quick Response”.

questions.description: The smallest coin in your piggy bank got a makeover, and a tough one.
questions.question: Today's 1-jiao (角) coin shows an orchid, is silver in color and stopped being made of aluminum in 2005. What is it made of now?
hints: The 2005 change made the coin harder-wearing and a bit heavier.
It's an alloy, a mix of metals, made mostly of iron.
It's the same metal as many kitchen sinks and spoons.
questions.fun_fact: It takes 10 jiao to make 1 yuan, so ten of these little orchid coins buy the same as one big 1-yuan coin.

questions.description: This torch travelled further than most families go on their summer holidays.

hints: It is often painted on old palace ceilings and embroidered on festive clothes.
It has nothing to do with animals or plants.
Look up at the sky on a sunny day and you may see the real thing.
questions.fun_fact: The Beijing 2008 torch was designed by a team from the Chinese computer company Lenovo.

hints: Its patterns are painted on before the glaze goes on, then fired.

Jay Chou has a famous song with this porcelain's name as its title.
questions.fun_fact: Jingdezhen got its name from the Song emperor Zhenzong, whose reign name Jingde (景德) was stamped on the town's porcelain made for the palace.

hints: Like the other lines of the song, it compares the girl to something from nature.

Xinjiang's Aksu region is famous for growing sweet ones of this fruit.
questions.fun_fact: Wang Luobin, called the “King of Western Folk Songs”, arranged this Uyghur song and made it famous all over China.

questions.description: A kitchen story so famous that philosophers still sharpen their minds on it.

hints: He lived during the Warring States period.

He once dreamed he was a butterfly and woke up unsure which one he really was.
questions.fun_fact: In Zhuangzi’s story, the cook used the same knife for 19 years and it was still as sharp as new.

The builders had to deal with floods, damp ground, snakes and wild animals.
The living space sat up in the air, with the ground left open below.
questions.fun_fact: Hemudu builders already joined wooden beams with mortise and tenon joints (榫卯), which hold together without nails.

questions.question: The Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (青藏高原) is called the “Roof of the World” (世界屋脊). What is its average height above sea level?
hints: No other large plateau on Earth is as high.
Many visitors get altitude sickness there, even when they stand still.
Lhasa, at about 3,650 m, actually sits lower than the plateau's average.
questions.fun_fact: The Qinghai-Tibet Plateau is still rising by a few millimetres a year, because the Indian plate keeps pushing into Asia.

They are famous for cold noodles and spicy pickled cabbage.
questions.fun_fact: Street signs in Yanji, the capital of Jilin's Yanbian prefecture, are written in both Chinese and Korean.

media.author: wanghongliu

questions.description: A goodbye poem where the only one waving might be the river.

hints: I lived in the Tang dynasty and spent much of my life travelling.

hints: It lies in western Inner Mongolia, in Alxa League (阿拉善盟).
Its UNESCO listing calls it a place of “towers of sand and lakes”.
It is the northwestern neighbour of the Tengger Desert.
questions.fun_fact: Some of Badain Jaran's dunes rise about 500 m (1,640 ft) above their base, and the lakes between them are fed by groundwater whose source scientists still debate.

Chinese people sometimes call themselves my descendants (龙的传人).
questions.fun_fact: In many tellings of the Great Race, the Dragon could have won but stopped to bring rain to a village, or to help the Rabbit across the river.

Du Fu was a younger friend of Li Bai and wrote in the middle part of the Tang dynasty.
The rebellion broke out in 755 and ended a few years later.

Its symbol is the black-and-white yin-yang circle (太极图).
questions.fun_fact: The Golden Hall on Wudang's highest peak was cast from bronze and covered in gold in 1416, during the Ming dynasty.

questions.question: In March 1938, German troops marched into Austria without a fight, and Hitler made it part of Germany. What is this called?
hints: It happened about a year and a half before the Second World War began in Europe.
Hitler himself was born in Austria.
The word means “joining” or “connection”.
questions.fun_fact: After the war, the Allies made Austria a separate country again.

questions.description: A spaceship with no room to stretch your legs for two weeks.
questions.question: This US spacecraft was photographed in orbit by another crew. Which NASA program did it belong to?
hints: Its missions flew in 1965 and 1966.
Its astronauts practiced spacewalks and meeting other craft in orbit, getting ready for the Moon.
Its name means “twins”, because each capsule carried two astronauts.
questions.fun_fact: In December 1965, Gemini 6A and Gemini 7 flew as close as about 30 cm (1 ft) to each other, the first crewed space rendezvous.

questions.description: This bird was flying errands for the gods long before it ever carried mail.
questions.question: Look at this bird. In Greek myth, it was the sacred bird of which goddess?
hints: Today this bird stands for peace, but for the Greeks it meant something else.
This goddess was born from the sea foam.
She was the goddess of love and beauty.
questions.fun_fact: In some ancient poems, the goddess of love rides through the sky in a chariot pulled by doves or sparrows.

questions.description: Music so calm that even the cello forgets to check its phone.
questions.question: Listen: what is the name of this famous slow piece for strings?
hints: You may have heard it at weddings, in commercials, or in films whenever a scene needs calm and elegance.
It comes from an orchestral suite written in the Baroque era by a German composer who also wrote many church cantatas.
Its nickname names one of the four strings on a violin.
questions.fun_fact: The nickname comes from an 1871 arrangement by violinist August Wilhelmj, who moved the melody so it could be played entirely on the violin's lowest string, the G string.
